chapter: Road shows in the Southwest and Midwest
title: Stranded in South Bend and taking over the Pastime Theater in Muskogee
summary: When Bailey's manager ran off with the money, Spikes was stranded in South Bend, then joined his brother in Muskogee and took over a failing theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, maybe we'll think of it later.

And, anyway, it went all up through Colorado,
and we finally left that, and we went to Muskogee to work in a theater
... No, before I get to that, this Bill Bailey troupe--when the manager run off and left us, my brother wasn't with us, but I stayed with
the show, and we got to South Bend, Indiana, and we all...after the
show, we come down the next morning to get on the train to go to
Hartford, I think it was, and no manager, no tickets, no money, and
we was all stranded there. And during that time, two or three of the
boys got jobs in the hotel as busboys and things. I got a job shining
shoes in a barber shop, and I took my saxophones over there one day

and was cleaning them and polishing them and everything, and the man fired me because he didn't want me loafing on the job, cleaning my saxophones and things. So... And my brother then was in Muskogee, Oklahoma, and he sent for me, and I got all of the rest of the boys to go, and we went to Muskogee, and we worked there for about three or four months, and the guy went broke, and so we took over the theater.
What was the name of the theater?
